title: Online task adaptation in functional-code space
hypothesis: Adapting a rank-2 task code preserves heldout task accuracy with fewer complete bytes and less adaptation work than updating a full local rule, while retaining previous task codes.
physical_object: shared 16D linear local rule with task-specific adaptation state
mirror_coordinate: per-task 2D code on a fixed shared basis
logical_multiplicity: 16 sequentially adapted task functions retained in state

development.selection_metric: test relative RMSE, actual complete serialized bytes, adaptation examples/ops, retained task count

fresh.reason: synthetic shared-subspace mechanism screen; no audit opened after native LoRA alias

paid_objects: all task codes or full task weights

compute.adaptation_solver: closed-form least squares; zero gradient updates

success_gate: At <=8 support examples/task, relative RMSE <=0.02; >=25% fewer complete bytes and adaptation ops than full task weights; retain all 16 prior tasks; strict gain over native LoRA control.
failure_gate: Quality/storage/adaptation gate miss or exact native low-rank adapter function/payload alias is FAIL for Mirror-specific value.
boundaries: Synthetic linear shared-subspace tasks only; fixed basis and base are supplied, not learned online.
Closed-form adaptation is not self-organizing NCA or end-to-end online learning.
No continual real-task retention or deployed runtime claim.
